parsed.why: Strong operating protections cover public accommodations and facilities, with refuge and care safeguards. National document, entry and custody risks still apply; suspended youth-care coverage and unresolved ballot measures limit the local uplift.

The state’s sex-at-birth policy backs gendered-space restrictions, and its court dismissed claims after a trans prisoner was assaulted in a men’s facility. The visitor’s exposure is less pervasive than explicit facility bans, but recourse and statewide protections are weak.

Public-accommodation protections, gender-identity hate-crime coverage, and enforceable shield laws provide the strongest local protections. No local facility ban is documented; national document, entry and custody exposures remain.

A birth-sex facilities ban covers public schools and government buildings, with an active complaint mechanism and no visitor-document exception established. Its scope is narrower than the private-venue ban in dossier 5; national risks also apply.

The facilities law reaches multi-occupancy public facilities, creates a cause of action, and operates amid weak statewide protections and documented hostility. Its broad reach makes exposure more pervasive than dossier 4’s government-building restrictions.
